venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner keeps FAU from sitting on Baugh. White keeps FAU from knowing who is rushing from the outside. FAU still moved the chains on the short throw Florida left open.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — combined condensed tape + GNFP Week 2. Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: Baugh is the night. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting extra men on him. Woods is how White messes with the tackle.

offense.body:
Buster Faulkner’s whole night is one job: do not let FAU decide in advance that the ball is going to Jadan Baugh.

If they do, they put extra people near the line and Baugh has nowhere to go. So Faulkner keeps changing who is standing where, and what the offensive line is pretending to do, until FAU is guessing. They can still go the other way without changing the play.

Here is what that looked like.

FAU is scared of Baugh, so they keep extra defenders close to him. That leaves Vernell Brown III with room. Philo throws him a short ball. First man misses. Brown runs 49 yards and scores. People will remember a long touchdown. It was a short throw and a missed tackle. That is Faulkner: you crept up for the run, he threw the easy one behind you.

The next trick is the fake run. Two tackles take off sideways like they are going to lead Baugh. FAU follows those tackles. The ball goes the other way — to Brown — and the three linemen in the middle are already out in front of him. Later it is Duke Clark, same idea, and those big people are already down the field when he scores from 10. You followed the fake. The ball went where you left.

If FAU does not bite — if they stay put and play Baugh — he runs it anyway. He scores from 12 with those same linemen actually leading him this time. In the third quarter everybody in the Swamp knows it is Baugh, and he still goes 61. Fourteen carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores. There were plays FAU sent extra people at the run, filled every hole, and he still ripped it. That is not Faulkner winning those plays. That is Baugh. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven men on him so those plays stay fair.

He also lines the receivers way out wide, and sometimes he puts Brown and Wilson one behind the other on that side. Now FAU has a bad choice. Crowd Baugh, and Brown or Wilson is alone with half the field. Spread out to cover those two, and Baugh is running against fewer people. That is why Brown’s night was not a trick-play night — the short throw, the screen, the 14, the 33. They kept using the room FAU gave them.

Sometimes Florida puts more players on one side of the field, then sends a man in motion across right before the snap. FAU is still counting who is where. Florida can still go the other way. They were late getting set all night.

One more look they will keep using: the tackle who is supposed to block the pass rusher instead takes off the other way, like it is a run. The rusher has to choose. Chase Philo, or honor the fake. Week one they showed that a lot and did not get a big play out of it. They will hand the ball off from that same look. Remember it when you see it.

Early on, Philo lined up with Baugh right behind him. They ran it, then they faked the run and Wilson sat down in the open grass for 19 yards. That look showed up once. It is not who they are. Wilson moved the chains all night because he finds the empty grass they leave him.

Philo ran the offense. He got them lined up. He snapped it with time on the clock. When they rushed him he kept his eyes downfield, stepped up, and still found somebody. He does not have to be the star. Stockton caught a ball that was a little late and still walked it in from the 11. Abrams’ 63 was the deep one when FAU finally crowded Baugh — the line looked like pass, not run, and Philo threw it over the top. Lead Abrams a step and he walks in. The interception is Micah Mays. The ball came off his hands. Sweeney was sitting there. When Philo holds the ball too long, the play dies.

The line is not blowing people off the ball. They are clean — almost no penalties, and the late defensive-line shift that wrecked them last year did not get them. They are also not getting out to the linebackers fast. The wide run they tried, they cannot run yet. Faulkner still shows it so FAU has to worry about the outside. What he does instead: he does not ask this line to block everybody. He leaves people unblocked on purpose and lets Baugh and the fakes do the rest.

The snaps over Philo’s head are Harrison Moore’s hands on a certain run block. Sumrall already said that. The one that lost twenty yards inside the five is the one that can lose a real game. The other miss: Philo ran it himself, FAU’s end was still there, lost two yards. The idea was fine. They lost the play.

Late, they block down the field like they mean it. Ten-yard runs become thirty. Micah Jones blows up one man, then the next, and they throw him the last touchdown. That is not a coincidence. Same idea as Clark’s score: get a big person in front of a skill player.

What Saturday was: a coordinator who will not let you sit on Baugh, a back you cannot tackle if they do not put extra men on him, and a quarterback who ran the offense. What to clean is the snap, the play where Philo ran it and got stood up, and the ball off Mays.
bullets: You creep up for Baugh, he throws the short one to Brown. That is the 49.
You follow the fake run, the ball goes the other way — Brown, later Clark.
You play it straight, Baugh runs it. The 12 and the 61.
Clean the snap, the play where Philo ran it and got stood up, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
FAU wants to throw it short until you step up and take that throw away. Florida never took it away.

The corners lined up several yards off the receivers. The linebackers did not step into that short area. FAU saw that before the snap, and then they got that throw anyway. Ninety plays. At one point they were 10-of-13 on third down. Henry and Valsin just kept catching the five-to-eight yard ball. Sumrall said it Monday: third-and-1, you cannot have your corner nine yards off. That happened. White will live with the short throw if Florida tackles. They did not tackle enough of it, and nobody was standing where that ball lands, so it became a long night.

He still has a real idea. He moves Jayden Woods so FAU’s tackle cannot get comfortable. Sometimes Woods is the man rushing from the outside. Sometimes he walks inside and somebody else has that outside rush. Mix it. Often. Do not leave him in one spot all night, and do not leave him alone out there if he starts chasing the quarterback.

When Veltkamp holds the ball, that idea pays. Coleman acts like the middle of the field is open, the ball goes outside, and Coleman is already there. That interception is a bait. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. He tips the next one. Dijon Johnson goes up and gets it. Same idea. Bett later beats the quarterback at the 1, the ball comes out, Johnson falls on it. McCloud stops them on fourth-and-2. The safeties were the part that looked like a staff — Coleman and Thornton. Kanye Clark played a real night in the slot and lost one ball to the corner of the end zone with no help over the top. That throw is the other side of lining up yards off the receiver. Valsin, 20 yards, touchdown. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

What they lost are the jobs inside the plan. The pile at the 1 — they had enough people, they lost the yard. Veltkamp walking in from 7 because the man on the outside left his spot. Woods is the guy who is supposed to stay there and keep the quarterback inside. When he chases, FAU ran at him. Later in the game Florida sent four rushers and still played the corners off. That takes away the deep ball. That also leaves the short throw and the throw to the corner alive.

They were ready for how fast FAU plays. They were not still looking at the sideline when FAU snapped it. Veltkamp is a real quarterback — he can throw it and he can run it. Sumrall called the defense atrocious at times because ninety plays and those fourth downs are what you get when the short throw is free.

Next week: stand where that short ball lands. Keep Woods on the outside when the quarterback runs it. Make him hold it. Coleman already showed you what that looks like.
bullets: The short throw was open. That is why FAU ran 90 plays.
White moves Woods so the tackle cannot get comfortable.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it.
Fix the pile at the 1, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

specials.body: The drive stalls. They take the points. Durkin from 53. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt is how the second Florida score starts.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt sets up the short field.

keys: Faulkner will not let you sit on Baugh. You creep up, he throws the short one. You follow the fake, the ball goes the other way. You play it straight, Baugh runs it.
Receivers out wide force a bad choice: extra men on Baugh, or room for Brown.
White moves Woods so the tackle cannot get comfortable. FAU still moved the chains because the short throw was open.
When Veltkamp holds it, Coleman and Johnson take it. Fix the pile at the 1, the man on the outside, and the throw to the corner.

nextWeek.look: Campbell will throw it short and the quarterback will run it. Sixkiller is their guy. Florida will still hand it to Baugh and keep changing how it looks. White has to stand on that short throw and keep Woods on the outside when Sixkiller runs it himself.
